HabitPulse is a simple habit tracking application designed to help users build consistency in their daily routines. Instead of focusing on complex productivity systems, the app allows users to easily add habits, track completion, and view daily performance in a clear and minimal interface.
Users can create their own habits such as studying, exercising, reading, or any personal goals. Each day, they can mark completed habits and receive a summary showing their progress and consistency level.
The goal of HabitPulse is to make habit building easy, visual, and motivating without unnecessary complexity.

Most people struggle with maintaining consistency in daily habits. HabitPulse solves this by giving users a simple system to track what they actually complete each day.
By visualizing progress and completion percentage, users can understand their discipline level and gradually improve over time. This encourages accountability and helps build long-term positive routines.
The app is especially useful for students and individuals trying to improve productivity, focus, and self-discipline in a structured but simple way.

HabitPulse allows users to create custom habits and track them daily using checkboxes. Each habit is stored locally on the device so it remains saved until the user deletes it.
At the end of the day, users can submit their progress to receive a completion score and feedback based on how many habits they finished. This helps users reflect on their productivity and improve consistency over time.
Users can also add or remove habits anytime, making the system flexible and personalized.

HabitPulse is a personal habit tracking tool intended for self-improvement and productivity tracking. It is not a medical or psychological application and should not be used as a replacement for professional advice.
All data is stored locally on the user device and is not uploaded or shared with external servers. Users are responsible for managing their own data and device security.
The app is provided as-is without guarantees of results. Habit improvement depends entirely on user consistency and engagement.
